name: Representation Theory

papers.title: Enhanced Helgason-Johnson bounds for classical groups of type $B$
papers.abstract: This paper improves the Helgason-Johnson bound in 1969 for non-Hermitian real classical groups of type $B$.

papers.title: On a new resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group E(2)
papers.abstract: We provide a non-divergent resolution of the identity for coherent states of the Euclidean group $E(2)$, replacing the integral on the whole group with the Haar measure by an invariant integration with non local kernels constructed by Steinberg and Wolf in 1981, valid for solutions of Helmholtz equation, that appears in natural way as the eigenvalue equation of the Casimir operator of $E(2)$. With this construction, all properties of Perelomov coherent states are preserved, in particular covariance, and all square-integrable functions are addmissible, improving previous results like those of de Bi\`evre and Torr\'esani.

papers.title: On generalized linear periods for inner forms of GLn
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{D}$ be a central division algebra of index $e$ over a non-Archimedean local field $\mathrm{F}$ of characteristic zero. For every integer $n\ge 1$ and every $s\in \mathbb{R}$, we classify the irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{D})$ that admit a nonzero linear form transforming under the subgroup $\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathrm{D})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(\mathrm{D})$ by the character $\nu^{es}\otimes\nu^{-es}$. We further show that such a linear form is unique up to scalars, and we characterize its existence in terms of Langlands parameters.

papers.title: Tensor ideals of oligomorphic permutation categories
papers.abstract: We classify tensor ideals for oligomorphic permutation categories $Perm(G,\mu)$. To this end we define an equivalence relation on the class of transitive smooth $G$-sets. We show that there is a bijection between the tensor ideals of $Perm(G,\mu)$ and the downward-closed subsets of the poset of equivalence classes. As a corollary we obtain that there is a bijection between tensor ideals and thick tensor ideals. We determine the poset in many cases (mostly in characteristic $0$): the infinite symmetric group, wreath products, products of oligomorphic groups, equivariantizations, finite groups in positive characteristic and the classical groups $GL, O, Sp, U$ over a finite field.

papers.title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts
The inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for groups of Lie type C
papers.abstract: We prove the inductive Galois-McKay conjecture for the symplectic groups. A key result is the determination of the character fields of the irreducible characters of the extensions of the symplectic group by field automorphisms. Two main ingredients for this are the theory of Brauer trees and the generalized Gelfand-Graev characters.

papers.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
papers.abstract: For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincar\'e pairing on $S^3/\Gamma$. In particular, $\Gamma$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

papers.title: Monoidal analog of cluster-tilting theory and monoidal reachability of acyclic cluster algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that many analogous facts of cluster-tilting theory holds in monoidal categories from quantum affine algebras or quiver Hecke algebras. We show that a maximal commuting family of real prime modules, which is an analogous object of a cluster-tilting object, is always a laurent family introduced by Kashiwara-Kim-Oh-Park. By using $\widetilde{\Lambda}$-invariants, we construct an exchange matrix of each laurent family and show that a laurent family is always completely $\Lambda$-admissible monoidal seed. We obtain that a pair of real prime modules is an exchange pair if and only if $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is $1$. When the category is a monoidal categorification of a cluster algebra of acyclic type, we prove that $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant is not less than generic Ext invariant by using tropical $F$-invariant introduced by Cao and Fei. Moreover, we show that, the conjecture asserting that real simple modules correspond exactly to cluster monomials holds in these cases.

papers.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge. Propagating this gap through the PBW filtration of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$, for every nonscalar element, we construct an alternating adjoint operator that lowers its order by exactly one. As applications, we compute the annihilators of all representations with nonzero central character, prove a strengthened form of Etingof's conjecture on nonsplit extensions of $W$-modules, and reduce the classification of prime ideals of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})$ to those of $\mathrm{U}(W)$.

papers.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group. We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.

papers.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.abstract: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Do\u{g}an and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026). To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019). Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

papers.title: The type I conjecture for locally compact groups acting on trees
papers.abstract: We prove that a closed group of automorphisms acting minimally on a locally finite tree and two-transitively on its boundary is uniformly admissible, hence of type I. This solves Nebbia's conjecture in a strong form. Together with the work of Caprace, Kalantar and Monod, this shows that for every closed nonamenable subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acting minimally on a locally finite tree $T$, $G$ is of type I if and only if the action on $\partial T$ is two-transitive. The key ingredient is the following operator algebraic result: if the projections of two atomic von Neumann algebras $A_1, A_2$ have integer traces, then every amenable amalgamated free product $A_1 \ast_B A_2$ with $B$ atomic is of type I.
